newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Details of sanctions, fines in EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Details of sanctions, fines in EMU stability pact.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Saturday agreed the terms of sanctions and fines to be imposed under the terms of a stability pact aimed at ensuring fiscal discipline within European Monetary Union.

Under the pact, countries which allow their annual budget deficits to exceed three percent of gross domestic product will normally face finanicial sanctions and later a fine, if no clear corrective action is taken.

The agreement between the finance ministers, reached at an informal meeting in Noordwijk, will form the basis of a legal text for the stability pact, which will be submitted for the approval of EU leaders at a summit meeting in June.

It foresees penalties up to a maximum of 0.5 percent of gross domestic product per year for those governments which overspend. Repeated offenders will face the penalties for each year for which they record an excessive deficit.
The following is an explanatory text on the agreed terms of the deal issued by the Dutch presidency. The text, which was released in English, is repeated here in full.
"Stability and Growth Pact - deposits and fines
1. If sanctions are applied, non-interest-bearing deposits would be required annually.
2. Two years after it was required, each deposit would be converted into a fine (if the excessive deficit has in the view of the Council not been corrected in the meantime).

* The amount of the first deposit shall comprise of a fixed component equal to 0.2 percent of GDP plus a variable component equal to one tenth of the difference between the deficit as a percentage of GDP in the preceding year and the 3 percent of GDP reference value.
* The amount of any subsequent deposit will be equal to one tenth of the difference between the deficit as a percentage of GDP in the preceding year and the three percent of GDP reference value.
* The maximum for any annual deposit is 0.5 percent of GDP."
